note: This batch was routed as a FIGURE batch, but pages 1211-1222 are Annex E (E.2 tail, E.3 Substantive changes probably not affecting existing programs). They carry NO general formats, syntax skeletons, railroad diagrams, or bracket/brace notation of any kind. The priority defect class for this run (lost choice indicators - the vertical bars just inside a bracket or brace per 5.2.6.4) therefore has zero exposure on these pages: there is no bracket, brace, ellipsis, or underlined required word anywhere in the batch. The pages are prose plus fixed-width Unicode code-point range listings. All code-point ranges were verified character-by-character against the rendered PDF (including the dense Arabic block on p1213, the Common block on p1214, the Inherited block on p1216, and the whole case-mapping table on p1222) and are transcribed correctly.

findings.markdown_says: Bopomofo:\n312D-312F, 31B8-31BF Brahmi:   (specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 49030)  ... then page-1214 opens with the bare line '11000-11046, 11066-1106F, 1107F' with no label
findings.why_it_matters: The 'Brahmi:' script label from the top of PDF page 1184 (md page 1214) has been concatenated onto the end of the Bopomofo range line on the previous page. Two entries are corrupted at once: Bopomofo's range line now reads '31B8-31BF Brahmi:', and Brahmi's code-point ranges are left orphaned at the head of the next page with no label at all. This is the E.3.3 item 5 list of characters newly permitted in user-defined words - the script-to-range mapping is exactly the data an implementer reads here, and the mapping is broken at this boundary.
findings.suggested_repair: Split line 49030 of specs/ISO_COBOL.md: leave '312D-312F, 31B8-31BF' as the Bopomofo range line at the end of page 1213, and move 'Brahmi:' to become the first content line of the page-1214 slice, immediately above '11000-11046, 11066-1106F, 1107F'.
